chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Ubaydah al-Hadda', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Bashfulness (al-hiya') is from faith (al-iman), and faith is in Paradise.

key_terms.الْحَيَاءُ: Bashfulness or modesty, a key moral virtue

ai.seo_question: What is the relationship between bashfulness and faith in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this foundational hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes *al-hiya* (bashfulness/modesty) not merely as a social virtue but as an intrinsic constituent of *al-iman* (faith), thereby grounding spiritual belief in tangible moral character. This linkage underscores the Shia scholarly view that true faith manifests through ethical conduct, with the ultimate reward being residence in Paradise, a concept deeply rooted in the Quranic description of the believers' attributes.
